findings.title: enableSqlExpressions() is dead logic that can never return true and misreads the feature flag
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (note the negation, which inverts the flag's meaning), then returns `false` in both the `if` branch and the fall-through. The feature-flag lookup result is therefore completely discarded and the function is a constant `false`. Even if the intent is to hard-disable SQL expressions, this shape is dangerous: a future reader will assume the flag is honoured and the inverted condition means a one-line "re-enable" change would turn the feature on when the flag is *disabled*. It is also the kind of ineffectual assignment that staticcheck/golangci can flag and break CI. Prefer an explicit `return false` with a comment referencing CVE-2024-9264, or remove the helper and return the error unconditionally.

findings.title: Disabled SQL expression returns a plain error with a misleading message
findings.body: When a `QueryTypeSQL` node is encountered the reader returns `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")`. Unlike the other error paths in this package (e.g. `NewSQLCommand` uses `errutil.BadRequest`), a bare error carries no status/public-message metadata, so an operator-enabled `sqlExpressions` toggle will surface as an opaque server error rather than a 400 with a clear reason. The wording is also misleading: the feature is intentionally disabled for security, not merely unimplemented, which will send users chasing a non-existent bug. Use `errutil.BadRequest` with a public message stating the feature is disabled.

findings.title: No regression test asserting SQL expressions are rejected
findings.body: This PR is a security fix (CVE-2024-9264) that disables server-side SQL expressions, but no test is added covering either entry point: `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` with `type: sql` (should error even with `FlagSqlExpressions` enabled) and `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`NewSQLCommand` (which now fails because `sql.TablesList` errors). Without such tests, a later refactor of `enableSqlExpressions` or of the `sql.DB` stub can silently re-enable the RCE/LFI path with no CI signal.

findings.title: TablesList is now permanently broken dead code that still contains the unsafe SQL string interpolation
findings.body: `TablesList` builds `SELECT json_serialize_sql('<rawSQL>')` by string concatenation with only naive `'` doubling and then calls `DB.RunCommands`, which the new stub in db.go always fails with `errors.New("not implemented")`. So the whole function can only ever return an error, and everything after line 26 (`tablesFromAST`, `astError`, `existsInList`, the `flatten` dependency) is unreachable. This leaves the exact query-construction code that was part of the vulnerability in the tree while providing no functionality, and any existing unit test asserting that `TablesList` extracts table names from a query will now fail. Either delete the parser together with the DuckDB removal or keep it behind a clearly-dead-code marker and update/remove its tests.

findings.title: tablesFromAST indexes ast[0] without a length check
findings.body: `flatten.Flatten(ast[0], ...)` will panic with an index-out-of-range if the deserialised AST JSON is an empty array (e.g. `[]`). The function is currently unreachable because `RunCommands` always errors, but if the DuckDB-backed implementation is ever restored this is an attacker-influenceable panic in a request path. Add a `len(ast) == 0` guard returning an error.

findings.title: Stub DB silently degrades SQLCommand.Execute into an opaque runtime error
findings.body: `NewInMemoryDB()` returns a struct whose `QueryFramesInto` always returns `not implemented`. `SQLCommand.Execute` (pkg/expr/sql_command.go:100-105) assigns that to `rsp.Error` and returns a nil error, so if any code path ever reaches execution (for example a query constructed without going through `NewSQLCommand`/`ReadQuery`) the user sees a bare "not implemented" in the query result instead of a clear "SQL expressions are disabled" message. Consider returning a descriptive, user-facing error from the stub that names the feature and the reason it is disabled.

findings.title: sqlExpressions feature toggle remains documented/registered while being a no-op
findings.body: `featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions` is still registered and documented as enabling server-side SQL expressions, but after this change enabling it has no effect other than producing an error on every SQL expression query. Operators who follow the existing docs will enable the toggle and get a confusing failure. The toggle's description (and the generated feature-toggle docs) should state that the feature is currently disabled/unavailable, or the toggle should be marked deprecated/hidden in this PR rather than deferred.
